text: Florida uses modified comparative fault now.
A plaintiff found more than 50 percent at fault recovers nothing, except in medical negligence cases.
Fault can be apportioned to a nonparty, called a Fabre defendant, if the defendant pleads it and proves it.
The dangerous instrumentality doctrine makes the owner of a motor vehicle vicariously liable when they entrust it to someone who drives negligently.
For slip and fall cases in a business, the transitory foreign substance statute requires proof of actual or constructive knowledge of the condition.
